security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements eidelivery CSR as writable (old spec: 'reset initializes to 0x20000000') instead of read-only fixed to 0x20000000 as required by the new spec when Smidctrl/Ssidctrl are present, allowing guest software to switch interrupt delivery mode away from ACLIC direct delivery
security_spec.summary: eidelivery CSR hardening: spec changes from reset-initialized to read-only-fixed 0x20000000 for ACLIC; writable implementation allows guest to break interrupt delivery path

findings.finding: eidelivery CSR is unconditionally writable via bit 0: the RMW function allows guest software to set or clear the delivery bit (wr_mask &= 0x1; imsic->eidelivery[page] = (old_val & ~wr_mask) | (new_val & wr_mask)). When Smidctrl/Ssidctrl are present (the ACLIC rework PR's target), the new spec requires eidelivery to be read-only fixed to 0x20000000. If this function is not gated on the absence of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl, a guest could switch interrupt delivery away from ACLIC direct delivery mode, causing denial of service.

eidelivery is reset to 0 via g_new0. When Smidctrl/Ssidctrl are present, the spec requires eidelivery to initialize to 0x20000000 (delivery enabled, direct delivery mode for ACLIC). A 0 reset value means interrupt delivery is disabled at boot, which would break guest interrupt handling when ACLIC is the delivery mechanism.

eidelivery is correctly used as a gate before signal assertion: if eidelivery[page] is 0, no external IRQ is raised even if a top-priority-enabled-pending interrupt exists. This is correct behavior for the current non-ACLIC spec where eidelivery acts as a per-file global enable bit.

CSR SIREG access to eidelivery ISELECT range is gated only by ext_ssaia presence and mvien/MIP_SEIP delegation check. There is no Smidctrl/Ssidctrl check here. When Smidctrl/Ssidctrl are present, writes to eidelivery via SIREG should either trap (illegal instruction) or ignore the write (WLRL read-only). Currently, the access is silently delegated to the IMSIC RMW callback which always honors writes.

eidelivery is correctly included in the VMState migration structure via VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32. This ensures live-migration preserves the delivery state across hosts. No missing-field risk for migration correctness.

The IMSIC register range (ISELECT_IMSIC_FIRST through ISELECT_IMSIC_LAST) correctly dispatches to machine-specific IMSIC emulation via env->aia_ireg_rmw_fn. Multi-hart indexing uses vgein for virtualized guest interrupt files and page 0 for non-virtual access. No illegal-info-leak path exists.

The siselect/miselect write path correctly uses ISELECT_MASK_AIA (0x1ff) to constrain select values, preventing out-of-range iselect values that could be abused to access unmapped IMSIC pages. WLRL constraint is properly enforced.

IMSIC realize correctly forces ext_ssaia/ext_smaia based on mmode, and registers the RMW callback via riscv_cpu_set_aia_ireg_rmw_fn. TCG and KVM paths are properly separated (RMW callback only registered for !kvm_irqchip_in_kernel). CSR side-effects are delegated to riscv_imsic_update() on every write.
